claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'EVALUATE statement, VI-84' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Conditional expression, VI-54'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'EVALUATE statement, VI-84' then '  Conditional expression, VI-54'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: The 300-dpi render of PDF page 966 (B-54, informative Index) shows a two-column index of one entry per line, sub-entries and wrapped continuations indented. The transcription holds every entry and page reference in the printed order (checked ERROR PROCEDURES through FILE-CONTROL and the second column), one entry per line, with sub-entries and continuations space-indented as printed. The source text and its line hierarchy are therefore intact. The claim concedes the entry text matches; its only complaint is how a Markdown renderer would collapse bare lines, compared with the list-marker style used on pages 961-962. That is a formatting and style inconsistency with no change of content or meaning, and the task rules reject a difference that is only formatting.
